name: touching_is_not_interpenetrating
why: THE TWIN OF `cover_inside_base`, and it proves the thing that case alone cannot prove: that the detection **does not answer one for everything**. Two plates resting face against face are a well-assembled assembly: if they came out as interpenetrating, the operation would shout on every correct assembly and one would learn to ignore it.
_why_this_case_counts_double: It also proves that **the argument `touching_counts` really changes the verdict**. The same two parts, in the same position, give ZERO with the default value and ONE when asking that coincidences count. Without this comparison the argument would be a knob nobody knows whether it turns: *an argument that changes nothing is worse than an argument that is not there, because whoever sets it believes they have decided something.*
_the_count_done_before: The base is 120x80x10 asked at y=0: `AddComponent5` places the CENTRE of the bounding box, so it occupies y from -5 to +5. The cover is 120x80x4 asked at y=7, so it occupies y from +5 to +9. **They touch exactly on the plane y=+5 and do not overlap at all.**
_and_what_touching_counts_is_really_for: A shaft inside a hole of the same diameter. There the coincidence IS the problem -- that part does not go in -- and with the default value it would come out fine. Two different questions on the same assembly, and the operation must be able to answer both.

expect.why: **THE REFERENCE, and it comes first.** Two plates resting on each other do not interpenetrate. If this were not zero, the twin case -- which demands one -- would prove nothing: it would only prove that the operation always answers the same number.
with which setting that zero was obtained

**A ZERO THAT DOES NOT EXPLAIN WHAT IT DID NOT LOOK AT IS A DANGEROUS ZERO.** Whoever reads «no interference» must know that the faces that touch were not in the count -- otherwise they send into production a shaft that does not fit in its hole believing they have checked it.

**THE SAME ASSEMBLY, AT THE SAME INSTANT, WITH ANOTHER QUESTION.** Zero in the previous step, one now: the argument changes the verdict, and it is the only way to show it. Two parts that share a face are well assembled if they are a cover, and are a part that does not fit if they are a shaft in a hole.
and the answer says with which of the two questions it was given

two calls in a row and the assembly is still what it was: the check touches nothing, and the detection is switched off after every run. If it stayed on, the document would stay in interference mode for whoever opens it afterwards.
